unresolved.what: Smolensk Governorate before Chernigov governorate was formed
unresolved.why: The lines with the Novgorod-Seversky namestnichestvo (1782), the Little Russian governorate (1796–1802) and the Polotsk/Mogilev/Belarus units are outside Den's change list, so the line before the 1802 units was not established.

unresolved.why: The lines with the Novgorod-Seversky namestnichestvo (1782), the Little Russian governorate (1796–1802) are outside Den's change list, so the line before the 1802 units was not established.

unresolved.what: Kursk Governorate before Chernigov governorate was formed
unresolved.why: Before 1797-08-29 O.S. (ПСЗ-1 № 18116) the line with Sloboda-Ukraine was moved by souls and villages (1779, and 1797-05-01 O.S.), not along 1897 uyezd lines. The lines with the Novgorod-Seversky namestnichestvo (1782), the Little Russian governorate (1796–1802) are outside Den's change list, so the line before the 1802 units was not established.
In 1782–1783 (ПСЗ-1 № 15343, 15485, 15656) parts of Borisoglebsk, Gvazda and Kirsanov circuits went to Saratov and Voronezh and part of Zadonsk came to Tambov: partial transfers through 1897 uyezds.

Tambov received Verkhnii Lomov, Kerensk, Nizhnii Lomov and Chembar uyezds of the partitioned Penza governorate and re-cut them with its own uyezds (1798); those 1780 uyezd lines are not 1897 uyezd lines, so the outline cannot be built.

unresolved.what: Nizhny Novgorod before the Kazan namestnichestvo
unresolved.why: The Kazan namestnichestvo was formed 1781-09-28 O.S. from the pre-reform Kazan governorate; Den gives only its uyezd list, so whether the Nizhny–Kazan line was re-drawn is not established.

unresolved.what: Nizhny Novgorod holding former Penza uyezds
unresolved.why: Krasnoslobodsk, Narovchat and Troitsk uyezds of partitioned Penza joined Nizhny Novgorod and were merged (1798); the Troitsk/Narovchat lines with Penza's other uyezds are not 1897 lines.

Penza namestnichestvo opened 1780-09-15 O.S. (ПСЗ-1 № 15061); its line with Saratov was set when the Saratov namestnichestvo opened 1780-11-07 O.S.; before 1780-09 the area belonged to pre-reform governorates.

From 1796-12-12 O.S. Penza held part of abolished Saratov governorate (renamed Saratov 1797), and from 1797-10-11 O.S. it was partitioned between four governorates; neither outline is a union of 1897 Penza uyezds.

Before 1796 and in 1796–1802 Voronezh had other lines (1797 parts of Bakhmut, Donetsk, Slavyansk; Boguchar and Ostrogozhsk in Sloboda-Ukraine); 1802–1824 it also held Starobelsk uyezd, which is in the Kharkov governorate atom group, so these atoms alone do not form it.
